title: Delhi Shivers As Temperature Drops To 17.1°C On Octobers Coldest Night, IMD Forecasts Clear Skies - Free Press Journal
full_text:
Delhi Shivers As Temperature Drops To 17.1°C On October's Coldest Night, IMD Forecasts Clear Skies
Delhi recorded its coldest October night on October 18, with the minimum temperature dropping to 17.1°C, according to the IMD. Lodhi Road and Ayanagar recorded 16.8°C each. Mainly clear skies and a maximum temperature of 32°C were forecast for October 19, while Delhi's AQI stood at 118.
Delhi recorded its coldest night of October so far on Sunday, with temperatures falling below normal across several weather stations. The IMD has predicted mainly clear skies on Monday, with the maximum temperature expected to reach 32°C.
New Delhi: Delhi recorded its coldest night of October so far on Sunday, October 18, as the minimum temperature dropped to 17.1°C, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The temperature was 1.3°C below the seasonal average, indicating cooler nights in the national capital.
The minimum temperature was also 1.5°C lower than Saturday’s reading. Several parts of the city reported temperatures below normal, with Lodhi Road and Ayanagar recording some of the lowest readings.
Lodhi Road, Ayanagar Record 16.8°C
According to the IMD’s observations released on Monday, October 19, Palam recorded a minimum temperature of 16.9°C, two degrees below normal. Lodhi Road and Ayanagar were slightly cooler at 16.8°C each, also two degrees below the seasonal average.
The Ridge weather station recorded a minimum temperature of 17.7°C, which was 1.8°C below normal. The readings show that the drop in night temperatures was not limited to one part of Delhi.
Clear Skies, Warmer Day Ahead
Despite the cooler nights, Delhi is expected to experience relatively warm conditions during the day. The IMD has forecast mainly clear skies, with the maximum temperature likely to reach 32°C on Monday, PTI reports.
Meanwhile, no rainfall was recorded at any of Delhi’s five weather stations during the 24-hour period ending at 8.30 am on Monday. The combination of cooler nights and warmer daytime temperatures highlights the contrast in the city’s weather conditions.

Delhi’s Air Quality Remains Moderate
Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 118 at 8 am on Monday, according to data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). This placed the city’s air quality in the ‘moderate’ category.
According to the AQI classification, a reading between zero and 50 is considered ‘good’, 51 to 100 ‘satisfactory’, 101 to 200 ‘moderate’, 201 to 300 ‘poor’, 301 to 400 ‘very poor’ and 401 to 500 ‘severe’.
While Delhi has recorded its coldest night of the month so far, the forecast of clear skies and a daytime high of 32°C suggests that the city will continue to experience a noticeable difference between day and night temperatures.

title: PETA India Urges Centre To Withdraw Draft Animal Experimentation Rules, Warns Of Weaker Safeguards - Free Press Journal
full_text:
New Delhi, October 19, 2026: Animal rights organisation People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals India (PETA India) has urged the Centre to withdraw its proposed rules on animal experimentation, warning that the changes could weaken existing safeguards and expose animals to greater suffering in laboratories.
The organisation has raised objections to the draft Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Control and Supervision of Experiment, Breeding and Trading of Laboratory Animals) Rules, 2026, claiming that several provisions could make it easier to conduct experiments on animals, including those protected under existing laws.
Protected Wildlife And Stray Animals At Risk
One of PETA India’s major concerns is that the proposed rules could permit the capture and use of animals protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, for experiments, provided scientific justification and legal permissions are obtained.
The organisation also warned that exemptions in the draft could allow experiments on stray dogs and cats under specified circumstances. These concerns raise questions about whether the proposed changes would offer sufficient protection to vulnerable animals.
Severe Suffering Remains A Concern
PETA India has also questioned provisions relating to the level of suffering permitted during experiments. It argued that while the draft prohibits prolonged severe suffering that cannot be relieved, it does not completely rule out experiments involving severe suffering.
“Although the draft prohibits prolonged severe suffering that cannot be alleviated, it continues to accommodate experiments involving severe suffering,” the organisation claimed.
Independent Oversight Could Be Weakened
Another key objection concerns the approval process for animal experiments. According to PETA India, the proposed rules could reduce the role of the central Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) in reviewing certain experiments.
“The draft would allow institutional ethics committees to approve experiments classified as mild or moderate on larger animals, including dogs, horses, pigs, and cattle, without prior approval from the central Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA),” it contended, PTI reported.
The organisation believes that allowing institutional committees to approve such experiments without prior clearance from the central body could weaken independent oversight and existing animal welfare safeguards.
PETA Pushes For Non-Animal Research Methods
PETA India also pointed to the global shift towards research methods that do not involve animals. It argued that the proposed rules should encourage scientifically advanced alternatives instead of creating more opportunities for animal experimentation.
The organisation said the focus should be on the “use of scientifically advanced non-animal approaches and animal-welfare protections, rather than weakening existing safeguards or creating new avenues for animal experimentation”.
Calls For Stronger Animal Protection Rules
Calling for the withdrawal of the draft, PETA India urged the Centre to introduce stronger regulations that protect wildlife and community animals while retaining independent supervision of experiments.

title: 2008 Ahmedabad Serial Blasts Case: Supreme Court Stays Execution Of Death Row Convict Mohammad Tanvir - Free Press Journal
full_text:
New Delhi, October 19, 2026: The Supreme Court has stayed the execution of the death sentence awarded to Mohammad Tanvir, an Indian Mujahideen operative convicted in the 2008 Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts case that claimed 56 lives and injured more than 200 people.
A bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh agreed to hear Tanvir’s plea challenging the Gujarat High Court’s July 7 verdict, which upheld the death sentences of 38 operatives of the terror outfit Indian Mujahideen.
Supreme Court Seeks Records, Stays Execution
“There shall be stay of execution of the death sentence awarded to the appellant (Tanvir),” the Supreme Court said in its October 9 order.
The bench directed that the original case records be obtained from the trial court and the high court.
It also instructed the Gujarat government to submit reports prepared by all probation officers concerning Tanvir within eight weeks.
The court asked the superintendent of the jail concerned to provide a report detailing the work Tanvir had undertaken during imprisonment, along with an assessment of his conduct and behaviour, within the same period.
“The superintendent of prison of the concerned prison shall also get done the psychological evaluation of the appellant from the government medical hospital,” the bench said, directing that the evaluation report also be submitted within eight weeks.
The Supreme Court scheduled the next hearing after 12 weeks.
High Court Upheld Death Sentences Of 38 Convicts
On July 7, the Gujarat High Court upheld the February 2022 judgment of a special court, which sentenced 38 convicts to death and 11 others to life imprisonment for their involvement in the serial blasts.
Rejecting the appeals filed by the convicts, the high court held that the criminal antecedents and individual roles of the 38 death row convicts established their involvement in a terrorist act warranting capital punishment.
The court observed that the special court had considered both mitigating and aggravating circumstances before awarding the sentences.
It cited the heavy loss of life, the “humongous nature of the conspiracy”, the intention “to create an atmosphere of widespread terror in the society”, the convicts’ conduct during the trial and the scale of the conspiracy as factors justifying the death penalty.
The high court also described the killings as an “inhuman and dastardly act” that had claimed innocent lives.
Ahmedabad Blasts Killed 56, Injured Over 200
On July 26, 2008, Ahmedabad was rocked by 21 bomb explosions across different parts of the city within 70 minutes, killing 56 people and injuring more than 200.
The investigation involved 35 police cases, including 20 connected to the Ahmedabad explosions and 15 concerning unexploded bombs recovered in Surat.
These cases were subsequently merged, leading to the trial of 78 people. The special court convicted 49 of them.
While confirming life imprisonment for 11 convicts, the Gujarat High Court observed that the prosecution had established their participation in terror-training camps and their involvement in procuring scooters, plastic containers and clocks used in the conspiracy. They had also arranged shelter for other individuals involved in the case.
The special court’s February 2022 judgment marked the first instance of a court sentencing 38 convicts to death in a single case.

Supreme Court Had Earlier Granted Relief To Another Convict
Tanvir is not the first convict in the Ahmedabad serial blasts case to receive a stay on the execution of his death sentence from the Supreme Court.
On October 1, the apex court had stayed the execution of Ahmed Bawa alias Abbu Abubakar Barelvi, another death row convict in the case.
With Tanvir’s appeal now before the Supreme Court, the execution of his death sentence will remain stayed while the court considers his challenge to the Gujarat High Court’s ruling.
